correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and f:Cr_n->{0,1,2}, the zero-defense inequalities are Y-y_i>=2 for zero a_i and X-x_i>=2 for zero b_i; every positive vertex needs a positive neighbor. Total weight <=3 forces one shore weight <=1, and either a zero on the opposite shore is indefensible or all its vertices positive and the unique selected matched pair has no selected neighbor. At weight 4, (1,3)/(3,1) fail by the same unmatched-positive obstruction, leaving X=Y=2. Then x_i=0 iff y_i=0, so supported indices coincide; totality excludes singleton support, and weight 2 per shore forces exactly two indices of four label-ones. Conversely each common pair is feasible. Thus gamma_{tR2}(Cr_n)=4 and exactly binom(n,2) distinct minima. Independent definition-level exhaustive checks of EVERY ternary labeling of weight <=4 for 3<=n<=6 match the complete asserted families, without replacing the arbitrary-n proof.
residual_risks: The theorem only classifies minima, not higher-weight Roman {2} functions.
n=2 is not part of the stated connected family though the analogous boundary can be checked separately.
